questions.answer: For the liquid slice, Δp = F/A. Its volume is AΔh, so its mass is ρAΔh and its weight is ρAΔhg. Therefore Δp = ρAΔhg/A = ρgΔh.
accepted_alternatives: An equivalent derivation using p_lower A - p_upper A = weight of the liquid slice.
questions.unit_policy: No unit is required for a symbolic derivation.

marking_points.text: Relates pressure difference to the resultant force on the liquid slice per unit area, using Δp = F/A or (p_lower - p_upper)A = F.
Writes the slice volume as AΔh and hence its weight as ρAΔhg.
Substitutes the weight into the pressure relation, cancels A and obtains Δp = ρgΔh.

parts.answer: The brine column between U and L has weight ρAΔhg. The pressure difference is this weight divided by area A, so Δp = ρAΔhg/A = ρgΔh and A cancels.
accepted_alternatives: An equivalent force-balance explanation using pressure forces p_L A and p_U A.
parts.unit_policy: No unit is required for the explanation.

parts.answer: Δp = 154 kPa - 118 kPa = 36 000 Pa. The separation is Δh = 36 000/(1120 × 9.81) = 3.28 m. Therefore the depth of L is 1.40 m + 3.28 m = 4.68 m.
accepted_alternatives: 4.7 m to two significant figures with valid working.
parts.unit_policy: The final depth must include metres.
